newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Early presidential election called in Montenegro.
newsitem.headline: Early presidential election called in Montenegro.

text.p: The speaker of the Montenegrin parliament, Svetozar Marovic, on Wednesday called presidential elections for October 5, practically three months before the mandate of incumbent President Momir Bulatovic expires.
Marovic said the election campaign in the smaller of the two republics which make up the rump Yugoslav federation should start immediately, the Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.
Nominations for presidential candidates are to be submitted to the republican electoral commission by September 15.
Bulatovic had wanted early parliamentary elections as the way to overcome the crisis in the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS).

Bulatovic was stripped of his post as party president earlier this month as a rift between reformists led by Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and hardliners in the DPS culminated. Bulatovic's hardliners maintain the sacking was illegal.
Marovic and most of the Montenegrin opposition are backing Djukanovic against Bulatovic who in turn enjoys support from Serbia, dominant partner in the federation.
Under the Montenegrin constitution, the president's mandate lasts five years and since Bulatovic was elected in January 1993, regular presidential elections were due in December this year.
Marovic's move to cut Bulatovic's mandate by three months is expected to be put before the Constitutional Court which is the only competent body to resolve this kind of dispute, Tanjug said.
